derivation: genitive case of an indefinite pronoun (some) otherwise obsolete (compare G4214 (πόσος));
def: as adverb of place, somewhere, i.e. nearly

occurrences.text: And being not weak in faith, he considered not his own body now dead, when he was about an hundred years old, neither yet the deadness of Sara’s womb:
But one in a certain place testified, saying, What is man, that thou art mindful of him? or the son of man, that thou visitest him?
For he spake in a certain place of the seventh day on this wise, And God did rest the seventh day from all his works.

source: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890) and Concise Dictionaries (1894), public domain; JSON by Open Scriptures (CC BY-SA).
